components.name: Query Router
components.role: Pre-processes user input, generating tokens for BM25 and embeddings for Vector search.

components.name: Keyword Retrieval Module
components.role: Executes BM25 algorithm against the inverted index for exact match and lexical relevance.

components.name: Vector Retrieval Module
components.role: Executes cosine similarity search against the dense vector index for semantic relevance.

components.name: Score Normalization Layer
components.role: Applies Min-Max scaling or Z-score normalization to align score distributions from disparate retrievers.

components.name: Fusion Engine
components.role: Combines normalized scores. Supports configurable weights (e.g., 0.5 BM25 + 0.5 Vector) or Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

components.name: Diversity Control (MMR)
components.role: Iteratively selects documents that maximize relevance to the query while minimizing similarity to already selected documents.

architecture.subtitle: One concept. Three AI perspectives. One tested architecture.
architecture.title: Hybrid Search Engine
architecture.workflow: 1. User Query -> Query Router. 2. Parallel calls to Keyword Module and Vector Module. 3. Results passed to Normalization Layer. 4. Normalized scores fused in Fusion Engine. 5. Fused list passed to MMR for deduplication. 6. Final list returned to user.

headline: Building a Hybrid Search Engine: Merging Keyword and Vector Retrieval
linkedin_post:
🚀 Just shipped the 'Hybrid Search Engine' reference slice for our Governed Enterprise RAG series!

We tackled the classic RAG dilemma: BM25 is great for exact matches, but vectors win on semantics. Why choose one when you can have both?

Our architecture uses a Score Fusion approach:
1️⃣ Parallel BM25 & Vector retrieval
2️⃣ Min-Max normalization
3️⃣ Weighted fusion (or RRF)
4️⃣ MMR for diversity control

This ensures we capture precise keywords without losing semantic context, all while avoiding redundant results.

Check out the full spec and implementation plan in the repo! 👇

#RAG #HybridSearch #AI #MachineLearning #SearchEngine #EnterpriseAI #OpenSource

data_flow: Ingest: Documents are indexed into both a keyword index (inverted) and a vector index (dense embeddings).
Query: User query is processed to generate both a keyword token list and a dense embedding vector.
Retrieve: Parallel execution of BM25 search and Vector similarity search.
Normalize: Scores from both retrievers are normalized to a [0, 1] range.
Fuse: Normalized scores are combined using a configurable weight parameter (alpha) or RRF.
Deduplicate: MMR algorithm is applied to the fused list to remove near-duplicates based on semantic similarity.
Return: Final ranked list of unique documents.
specification.description: A production-ready reference slice demonstrating a Hybrid Search Engine that fuses BM25 (keyword) and Dense Vector (semantic) retrieval results. The system addresses the limitations of single-modal retrieval by leveraging score normalization, weighted fusion, and diversity control (MMR) to provide robust, non-redundant search results.
specification.series: From RAG to Governed Enterprise Agents

technical_requirements.fusion_algorithm: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or Weighted Linear Combination with Min-Max normalization
technical_requirements.keyword_engine: BM25 implementation via Whoosh or Elasticsearch
technical_requirements.vector_engine: Dense embedding model (e.g., BGE, E5) with FAISS or Pinecone index

specification.title: Hybrid Search Engine Reference Implementation

takeaway: Hybrid search is not just about running two retrievers; it's about how you combine them. The key engineering challenge lies in score normalization and diversity control. By using Min-Max normalization and Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR), we mitigate the redundancy inherent in fusing two high-recall systems, resulting in a more precise and user-friendly search experience.
validation_method: External peer scores only (no self-scoring). Average of two anonymous reviews. Blockers for unsupported claims, fabricated references, critical security flaws. Model agreement alone does not certify correctness.
